outputs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original Citadel Pikeward tactical-game sprite poses, using the supplied original artwork as identity and painterly style reference: male soldier, steel helmet with red plume, segmented red and steel armor, cream scarf and cream-red skirt, teal cloth panel, tall red/cream shield with original riverwave brass sun decoration, long hooked steel polearm. Exactly twelve full-body separately articulated poses in a roomy 4-column by 3-row sheet. All face RIGHT in consistent three-quarter camera. Row 1: relaxed idle with polearm near vertical; breathing idle with free shoulder and head slightly shifting; walking contact one foot ahead shield carried; narrow passing step other boot beside supporting ankle. Row 2: pulling polearm back to wind up a thrust; thrusting polearm horizontally RIGHT with shield forward, rear heel raised; crouched planted shield guard; recoiling behind shield under impact. Row 3: sinking onto one knee with shield sagging; collapsing onto side with weapon slipping down; fully prone dead body with shield and polearm resting alongside; opposite walking contact with other leg ahead. Same body scale in every cell, including corpse. Generous empty gutters and margins; entire long polearm fits in its cell without overlapping neighboring artwork, keep head/body size consistent even when weapon extends. Real changes in joints, hands, limbs and equipment, not transformed copies. Flat uniform green RGB(0,255,0) background including gaps, no ground/shadow, text, frame lines, effects or blood. Original raster painting, no borrowed copyrighted artwork.
outputs.alpha_prompt: Remove the green background from this sprite sheet. Preserve the twelve characters and their equipment unchanged. Return them isolated on a transparent background.
